cat << 'EOF' > generate_plot.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Create the figure and axis
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Define the broken bars
# First broken bar (blue)
broken_bar_1 = [(98, 28), (128, 47)]
broken_bar_2 = [(8, 46), (99, 22), (132, 15)]

# Plot the first broken bar (blue)
ax.broken_barh(broken_bar_1, (10, 11), facecolors='blue')

# Plot the second broken bar (orange, green, red)
# We need to plot each segment separately to set different colors
# Segment 1: orange
ax.broken_barh([(8, 46)], (20, 11), facecolors='orange')
# Segment 2: green
ax.broken_barh([(99, 22)], (20, 11), facecolors='green')
# Segment 3: red
ax.broken_barh([(132, 15)], (20, 11), facecolors='red')

# Set labels and title
ax.set_xlabel('seconds since start')
ax.set_yticks([10.5, 20.5])  # Center of the bars
ax.set_yticklabels(['Bill', 'Jim'])

# Enable grid lines
ax.grid(True)

# Add annotation for "race interrupted"
ax.annotate(
    'race interrupted',
    xy=(55, 28),
    xytext=(0.7, 0.8),
    textcoords='axes fraction',
    arrowprops=dict(facecolor='red', shrink=0.05),
    fontsize=10,
    color='red'
)

# Set axis limits to ensure all bars are visible
ax.set_xlim(0, 150)
ax.set_ylim(0, 32)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
EOF
